options: A hosting plan for static websites
A service offered by an application to enable communication and data exchange at an application level
A browser plug-in for viewing XML
A physical server located in a data centre
questions.explanation: A web service is a service offered by an application to enable communication and data exchange at an application level.

questions.stem: Which two types of web services are mainly used when integrating applications?
questions.explanation: The two main types of web services used for application integration are REST and SOAP.
REST stands for Representational State Transfer, a software architecture style for designing and communicating web applications.

questions.stem: Why are sessions not required by REST web services?
options: Because REST only supports the GET method
Because REST runs only on private networks
Because REST employs a stateless protocol in a client-server architecture
questions.explanation: REST web services employ a stateless protocol in a client-server architecture, so sessions are not required.

questions.stem: Which HTTP method is described as safe because it is read-only and cannot change the target resource?
questions.explanation: GET retrieves a representation of the target resource; it is safe because it is read-only, and it is also cacheable.

questions.stem: Which data format is the most used with REST web services?
questions.explanation: REST web services can use multiple data formats such as JSON or XML, but JSON is the most used.

questions.stem: Which data format does SOAP use for its messages?
questions.explanation: SOAP uses only XML formats in predefined schemas; SOAP messages are XML documents encapsulated in an envelope.

questions.stem: In a SOAP message, which part is optional and may carry authentication credentials?
questions.explanation: The header is an optional part of a SOAP message; it can carry information such as authentication credentials and definitions of complex types.

questions.stem: What is WSDL sometimes referred to as?
questions.explanation: WSDL provides a complete description of a web service's operations and parameters and is sometimes referred to as the web service signature.

questions.stem: Which description language is described as the REST-side counterpart of WSDL for SOAP?
questions.explanation: WSDL for SOAP is described as somehow equivalent to WADL for REST web services; both are XML-based.
